findings.summary: The prior final review's sole REJECT finding (rf-03a36b4d: version-bound review validation and delivery not synchronized with version activation) is addressed. GoalRequestKernel now holds a per-kernel _version_lock (threading.RLock): activate_version persists and activates a version under it, and finish_goal_call admits and delivers approve/reject under the same lock (the whole business-guard read through the external port call is one critical section). A concurrent activation therefore cannot land between reading the active version and the review reaching the port. The barrier-controlled offline regression test_concurrent_version_activation_is_excluded_from_review_delivery pins this with threading.Barrier/Event: activation stays parked while review delivery is in flight and completes only after the critical section releases.

Goal version activation remains unwired into the production composition path: build_line constructs GoalRequestKernel without calling activate_version, so active_version stays empty until a live Goal/version event arrives. The explicit-version and stale-version-refusal semantics are fully implemented and offline-tested against an explicit active_version; wiring a goal content_revision -> activate_version source is deferred integration consistent with the spec's explicitly deferred later slices (full MCP enroll/repo lifecycle, live binding), not a development-stage violation. Unchanged by this attempt.

input_commit, subject_commit, and implementation_subject_commit are all 6ddd7bffb27b311ea33061e61cf9c10a4a19c613 as supplied, satisfying the equality contract. work_head_commit 7c2ca19775e10e6b9946a5be78ace4fe6129a466 differs only as the top-of-tree of a metadata-only materialization; mechanical byte-equivalence of the product tree (git diff excluding .dev-dispatch) could not be executed with the available read-only file-inspection tools, and no shell or Git command was run.
